Counsel for Applicant :- Shailesh Sachan,Gaurav Singh,Piyush Agnihotri,Sachin Kumar Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Saurabh Lavania,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material on record.
Present application has been filed by the applicant for the following main reliefs:-
"I. That prayer to Quash or modify the unreasonable condition imposed by the Learned Judicial Magistrate III, Lucknow in order dated 18.12.2024 passed by Learned JM- III, Lucknow in Application for permitting to continue with his employment abroad in persunace of criminal case no.267 of 2023, State of U.P. vs.
Keshav Krishna Mishra vs State Of U.P. Thru. Home Deptt. Lko. on 7 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/139218808/
1 Keshav Krishna Mishra & others, Case crime no. 0035/2021, under section 498A,
323, 504, & 506 Indian Penal Code, and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police station- Mandion,
District- Lucknow pending before learned Judicial Magistrate III, Lucknow contained as Annexure no. 1, in the interest of justice.
II. That this Hon'ble Court may allow the applicant to travel abroad to continue with his employment without putting so grave and unreasonable condition on the applicant in the interest of justice."
It is stated that the Judicial Magistrate-III, Lucknow vide order dated 18.12.2024 has allowed the application preferred by the applicant inCase Crime No. 0035 of 2021, under Sections- 498A, 323,
504, 506 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police station- Mandion, District- Lucknow with the direction to submit/furnish personal bond of Rs. 5,00,000/- (Rs. Five Lakhs Only) and two reliable sureties each of the like amount.
However, applicant is not in a position to satisfy the said condition.
Taking note of aforesaid as also the observations made by the Hon'ble Apex Court on the condition of bail in the case(s) of Moti Ram and Others vs. State of Madhya Pradesh (1978) 4 SCC 47,
Hussainara Khatoon and Others vs. Home Secretary, State of Bihar, Government of Bihar, Patna;
(1980) 1 SCC 81; Hani Nishad @ Mohammad Imran @ Vikky vs. State of U.P. in Special Leave to Appeal (Crl.) 8915 of 2018; Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another (2022) 10 SCC 51; Guddan @ Roop Narayan vs. State of Rajasthan (Criminal Appeal No. 120 of 2023 @ SLP (Criminal) No. 9756 of 2022); In Re: Policy Strategy for Grant of Bail (SMWP (Criminal) No. 4/2021); Munish Bhasin and Others vs. State (Government of NCT of Delhi) and Another (2009) 4 SCC 45; Sanjay Chandra vs. Central Bureau of Investigation (2012) 1 SCC 40;
Sandeep Jain vs. National Capital Territory of Delhi (2000) 2 SCC 66 as also the judgment passed by the Karnataka High Court in case of Afsar Khan vs. State; I.L.R. 1992 KAR 2894 and the judgment passed in case of Sagayam @ Devasagayam vs. The State of Tamil Nadu; 2017 (3) CTC 291 and Sundar @ Ashok vs. Inspector of Police, T-16 Nazarathpet Police Station (Crl. O.P. No. 993 of 2017 dated 18.01.2017) by the Madras High Court, according to which, onerous condition and also heavy amount as surety should not be imposed, this Court is of the view that the order dated 18.12.2024 is liable to be modified only to the extent of furnishing a personal bond of Rs. 25,000/-
(Rs. Twenty Five Thousands Only) and two sureties of the like amount.
